rows.title: Amberes 64 Ascend Hotel Collection
rows.body:
Urban boutique, Mexico, CALA, Conversion, Zona Rosa

Mexico City, Mexico (Zona Rosa / Colonia Juárez)

Conversion / repositioning · 64 suites · kitchenettes, restaurant, bar, gym, steam

Choice Hotels CALA inaugurated Amberes Seis Cuatro Ascend Hotel Collection on 29 July 2024 in Mexico City's Zona Rosa—steps from Ángel de la Independencia. Press describes luxury suites with kitchenettes, restaurant and bar, fitness center, steam area, and game lounge in a 1967 building repositioned under the industry's first soft brand.

Ascend fits owners who want to keep a distinctive urban boutique story while gaining Choice Privileges, CRS distribution, and CALA development support—not a rigid prototype limited-service box.

Use for CALA independent conversion: collection compliance versus local character, F&B retention, and Zona Rosa transient + corporate mix. Verify fee stack, PIP scope, and ramp locally.

https://www.choicehotels.com/mexico/mexico-city/ascend-hotels/mx228
rows.caseSummaryOverview: July 2024: Amberes 64 / Amberes Seis Cuatro Ascend in Mexico City Zona Rosa—64-suite boutique conversion with kitchenettes, restaurant, bar, gym, and steam under Choice Hotels CALA inauguration press.
rows.caseSummaryOwnerObjective: Preserve a distinctive Zona Rosa boutique identity while accessing Choice distribution, loyalty, and collection standards—not a greenfield prototype play.
rows.caseSummaryBrandRelevance: Illustrates Ascend as CALA soft-collection conversion for independent upscale assets with local F&B and design character retained within membership criteria.
rows.caseSummaryInterpretation: Model conversion CapEx, collection PIP timing, and urban comp-set supply before treating inauguration press as performance proof.

rows.title: Grand Hotel Guayaquil Ascend Hotel Collection
rows.body:
Historic, Ecuador, CALA, Urban full-service, Waterfront

Guayaquil, Ecuador

Conversion · landmark hotel · meetings and F&B

Grand Hotel Guayaquil operates as an Ascend Hotel Collection member on the Guayaquil waterfront—historic full-service character with Choice consumer distribution in a key Ecuador gateway.

Ascend enables a landmark independent to keep its local story while participating in Choice Privileges and enterprise channels—distinct from hard-brand Cambria or midscale flags.

Owner lens: heritage conversion with collection flexibility—diligence preservation costs, F&B complexity, and waterfront/leisure vs. corporate mix.

https://www.choicehotels.com/ecuador/guayaquil/ascend-hotels/ec002
rows.caseSummaryOverview: Guayaquil waterfront: Grand Hotel Guayaquil Ascend Hotel Collection—historic full-service member on choicehotels.com in Ecuador's primary business gateway.
rows.caseSummaryOwnerObjective: Retain landmark hotel identity and F&B positioning while adding Choice loyalty and distribution—not homogenizing to a single prototype.
rows.caseSummaryBrandRelevance: CALA Ascend proof point for historic urban full-service conversions versus select-service hard brands.
rows.caseSummaryInterpretation: Heritage PIP and preservation economics dominate returns—use for collection-fit narrative, not audited performance.

rows.title: Ascend Hotel Collection — Quito historic capital
rows.body:
Urban heritage, Ecuador, CALA, Boutique, Capital gateway

Quito, Ecuador

Soft collection · historic core adjacency

Ascend member property in Quito illustrates collection placement in an Andean capital—local character with Choice network access for international and domestic travelers.

Use when the owner story is "independent or boutique upper-upscale in CALA capital → collection membership without losing place-based identity."

Compare altitude-market seasonality, access patterns, and collection compliance scope before underwriting.
